title: UK house prices rise 0.2% in August, ending decline
summary:
UK house prices increased 0.2% month-on-month in August to reach an average of £275,465, according to Nationwide, marking the first monthly rise since April. The rise follows a three-month decline as the market awaits the Bank of England's interest rate decision on 17 September.

title: Lender completes £1.1m bridge for Denton food hall in a week
summary:
Roma Finance has provided a £1.1m commercial bridge loan to Hatters Square Limited, the property holding company behind a food and drinks hall on Market Street in Denton. The facility was structured at 55% loan-to-value against the property's £2m market value, completing within seven days.

title: Multi-lender refinance unlocks £1.1m from Reading conversion
summary:
FRP Real Estate Advisory has arranged a £1.1 million refinance on a completed office-to-residential conversion in Reading, spanning four lenders and seven separate leases. The transaction will fund the client's next conversion project in the South East.

title: UK property transactions decline 2% in July 2026
summary:
UK residential property transactions fell by 2% in July 2026 compared to the previous month, according to HMRC data, as the summer period dampened market activity. The latest property transactions data shows that on a seasonally adjusted estimate, the number of residential transactions in July 2026 was 96,710.

title: Dwelly completes tenth estate agency acquisition of 2026
summary:
Estate agency consolidator Dwelly has acquired Paramount Properties, a London-based estate and lettings agency, marking its tenth acquisition in 2026. The transaction adds approximately 1,100 fully managed properties to Dwelly's network, bringing its total portfolio to more than 15,000 properties under management.

title: Right to Buy debate intensifies over council housing policy
summary:
A debate over Right to Buy policy has intensified as the government considers requiring 10 years of tenancy before purchase and protecting new social homes from the scheme for 35 years. Industry figures argue restrictions could create a permanent rental class rather than addressing housing shortages.

title: Government launches approved trader code for home improvements
summary:
The Government has introduced an Approved Code scheme for tradespeople, aimed at addressing consumer protection issues in the home improvement sector. Research shows more than one in four adults who undertook home improvements in the past 18 months encountered problems, with consumers losing over £10.3 billion in 2024.

title: Spicerhaart commits £1.7m to bespoke management platform
summary:
Estate agency group Spicerhaart has invested £1.7 million over five years in a customised property management system developed with software provider Rex. The platform, developed over two years, aims to address regulatory changes including the Renters' Rights Act.

title: Cleverly steps down as Shadow Housing Secretary for mayoral bid
summary:
Sir James Cleverly has resigned from his position as Shadow Housing Secretary to pursue the Conservative candidacy for London Mayor in the 2028 elections. The Conservative MP for Braintree, who held the shadow housing role since July 2025, announced his intention to run for the mayoral position over the weekend.

title: School catchment areas add £40,000 to property prices
summary:
Properties located near top-performing state secondary schools in the UK command an average premium of £40,574, representing an 11% increase over comparable homes in surrounding areas. The research shows price differentials that can rival private education costs, with significant regional variations.
